cd /tmp && grep -n "(K−1)/K\|(K-1)/K" storywiki2/Outline.md | cut -c1-80; cat > i.md <<'EOF'
Brief rev. 7 (idea-repo) corrected the break-even factor after paper-repo #4: **n\* ≈ K/(K−1) · d_eff σ²_res/Δ**, not d_eff σ²_res/Δ·(K−1)/K. I re-derived it: with K folds the calibrator is fit on n_train = (K−1)n/K labels, so its learning cost is d_eff σ²_res/n_train = d_eff σ²_res·K/((K−1)n); setting this equal to Δ (the common factor (1/n−1/M) cancels) gives n\* = K/(K−1)·d_eff σ²_res/Δ. The corrected form is the one to use.

Outline rev. 2 still carries the old factor in the C3 row (section 2) — `n\* ≈ d_eff σ²_res/Δ·(K−1)/K`. Please update it to Brief rev. 7. The pre-fixed factor-3 tolerance is unaffected for K=5 (the factor is 1.25 vs 0.8) but the predicted n\* that the grid must bracket shifts by that factor. Brief rev. 7 also writes the excess as Var(m−g) rather than E(m−g)², and Δ = Var(m(f) − a\* − b\*f); both identical under the intercept-free fit, so no change in claims. I checked the algebra, including the correlation-ratio form V\* = (Var Y/n)(1 − η²N/M).
EOF

shown.message:
I opened `story-repo`#4 asking `story-repo` to update the break-even factor in the Outline's C3 row. The rest of Brief rev. 7 needs nothing from me.

- **The correction:** Brief rev. 7 changes the break-even n from d_eff·σ²_res/Δ·(K−1)/K to **K/(K−1)·d_eff·σ²_res/Δ**. I re-derived it independently and the new form is right. With K folds the calibrator learns from (K−1)n/K labels, so its learning cost is d_eff·σ²_res·K/((K−1)n), and setting that equal to Δ gives the new factor.
- **The Outline still carries the old factor:** it appears in C3 of rev. 2. For K=5 the predicted n shifts by a factor of 1.56, which matters for the rule that the n-grid must bracket the predicted break-even.
- **Other changes in rev. 7:** I checked the new correlation-ratio form of the variance floor and it also holds. Writing the excess as Var(m−g) instead of E(m−g)² changes no claim.

Nothing is owed to `idea-repo`.
